messages:
maya: Heads-up — seeing quota spikes in the canary for routing policy `auth-routing:sparse`. Dashboard sparkline jumped ~5x at 16:10 but billing meter doesn't reflect the same increase. Looks like traffic is being attributed to org keys rather than the service-account that actually called. Anyone else see this?
adrian: Hm, I saw a short blip on the X-ops metric earlier but assumed sampling noise. Can you paste the query you used for the sparkline?
maya: Yep — pulled raw counts from the telemetry store:
```
SELECT time_bucket('1m', ts) as minute, origin_key, effective_identity, sum(requests) as cnt
FROM metrics.auth_requests
WHERE policy = 'auth-routing:sparse' AND ts >= now() - interval '1h'
GROUP BY minute, origin_key, effective_identity
ORDER BY minute DESC
```
This shows most of the extra rows tagged with origin_key=org_123 but effective_identity=sa:billing-worker. The dashboard widget only surfaces origin_key so it's misleading.
zara: That matches what we saw in the last rollout — console widgets are still pinned to the high-level origin header. Sampling + grooming can hide the SA-level attribution. We need a quick UX tweak to show an "effective identity" pill in the sparkline hover.
cheng: Short-term ops fix: when we compute quota usage for Dedicated customers we should switch attribution to `effective_identity` if present, fallback to `origin_key` only if missing. That will preserve historical billing while fixing miscounts going forward.
adrian: I can run a reconciliation job to estimate the delta if we re-attribute by identity. Quick test: run the same query but `GROUP BY effective_identity` only and compare 24h totals. If delta > 2% we treat as material.
maya: Thanks — can you run it and post numbers? We need to decide whether to patch the canary (rollback vs tweak attribution) tonight.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: auth-router-v2 -> canary(10%). SHA: abc123 — 16:12 UTC.
zara: Ugh timing. If the canary is the source, we should pause further rollouts until we confirm. Can we flip the canary to 0%?
cheng: We can toggle sampling in the router but that takes ~30s to propagate. I'll hold off until adrian posts reconciliation.
adrian: Ran quick compare. 24h totals grouped by origin_key vs effective_identity: origin_key=org_123 => 12,450 requests; effective_identity=sa:billing-worker => 11,980 requests; other org_keys sum => 470. Delta ~3.8% (some traffic truly originated elsewhere). Looks like attribution will shift ~3.8% of usage away from org-level billing to SA-level.
maya: That's material for the org but also fixes the console mismatch. Proposal: patch dashboard widget to include effective_identity next to origin_key, and update quota aggregation to prefer effective_identity for canary traffic only (so we don't surprise production billing). Then run a reconciliation window for 48h to validate.
zara: UX suggestion: show a small warning pill on the dashboard when attribution mode differs from billing mode: "Attribution = SA (canary) vs Billing = Org" with a link to docs.
adrian: +1 on staged approach. I can produce the reconciliation numbers and a migration plan. I'll open an internal PR to the metrics pipeline with a feature flag `prefer_identity_for_canary` and a console flag to expose the pill.
cheng: I'll handle the router toggle if we need to pause. Also suggest we add a unit test that ensures metric tags include both `origin_key` and `effective_identity` for downstream consumers.
maya: Cool. Owners: adrian (recon + pipeline PR), zara (console UX patch + pill), cheng (router toggle + tests). I'll create the follow-up ticket and tag you. Please add ETA to the ticket — want a rollback plan if anything weird shows up after the reconciliation.
adrian: ETA for initial PR + numbers: 6h. Will post results here.
zara: I'll mock the pill in the console preview and share screenshots before the PR merges.
maya: Thanks. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Canary updated: auth-router-v2 -> canary(0%) by cheng — 16:28 UTC.
adrian: Reconciliation posted in ticket #INF-4282 — numbers attached. Early look: attribution shift consistent with the quick run.
maya: Great, leaving this thread open until we confirm the pipeline flag and console patch are live. Keep pinging here for blockers.
